options.systemMessage:
You investigate why an application broke on a server. You can only read, never change anything.
Work in this order:
1. Call list_app_containers to see every part of the app.
2. For every container that is not running, call read_container_logs and container_state.
3. If a log points to another part, a file, the disk or memory, check that too (query_metrics, check_endpoint).
Never state a fact you did not see in a tool result. Never mention a container that list_app_containers did not show.
Only when you are done, reply with this JSON and nothing else:
{"cause": "one or two sentences: what broke first and why the rest broke",
 "root_container": "the container where the problem starts",
 "evidence": ["text copied exactly from a tool result", "..."],
 "checked": ["what you checked"],
 "next_steps": ["up to 3 concrete steps for the developer"]}

parameters.toolDescription: Lists every container of the broken app with its state and status. Use it first to see which parts are down.
Reads the last 60 log lines of one container. Input: the container name exactly as listed.
Shows how a container ended: state, exit code, OOMKilled, start and stop time, restart count.
Runs a PromQL query on Prometheus for the server metrics, e.g. node_filesystem_avail_bytes, node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes, up.
Calls an HTTP endpoint of the app on this server with GET, e.g. port 3000 path /health. Shows what users would get.

parameters.query:
WITH input AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS j),
created AS (
  INSERT INTO incidents (fingerprint, app, root_container, cause_type, title, cause, evidence, affected, next_steps)
  SELECT j->>'fingerprint', j->>'app', j->>'root_container', j->>'cause_type', j->>'title', j->>'cause', j->'evidence', j->'affected', j->'next_steps'
  FROM input WHERE j->>'action' = 'new' RETURNING id)
SELECT id FROM created
UNION ALL SELECT (j->>'open_id')::int FROM input WHERE j->>'action' = 'notify';
UPDATE incidents SET last_seen = now(), occurrences = occurrences + 1 WHERE id = $1 RETURNING id, occurrences;

UPDATE incidents SET investigation = j->'investigation',
  cause = CASE WHEN j->>'cause_type' = 'found_by_investigation' THEN j->>'cause' ELSE cause END,
  evidence = j->'evidence', next_steps = j->'next_steps'
FROM (SELECT $1::jsonb AS j) s WHERE id = (j->>'incident_id')::int RETURNING id;
UPDATE incidents SET status = 'resolved', resolved_at = now(), resolved_note = $2 WHERE id = $1 RETURNING *;
UPDATE incidents SET emailed_at = now() WHERE id = $1 RETURNING id;

parameters.content:
## 1. Scan
Every minute: list all containers through the read-only Docker proxy and keep the broken parts of apps that are running.

## 2. Find the cause
Read how each container ended and its last 200 log lines, then follow the app's dependencies to one root cause.

## 3. Report once
New incident: save it, email the developer, mark it as emailed. Known incident: only count it.

## 4. Close fixed incidents
Healthy again, or the whole app switched off: close the incident and send a short email.

## Optional: AI investigation
Only when the rules cannot explain an error. A local model reads logs and states through read-only tools. Quotes it did not really see are thrown out.
